bull.t: China regulatory approval expands etripamil’s commercial pathway
bull.b: China’s first approval outside the United States validates etripamil’s clinical and regulatory profile while opening a partner-led commercialization route. The milestone payment, potential development and commercial milestones, and tiered royalties could create durable international revenue leverage if regional adoption develops.

bull.t: Early launch adoption and formulary access are improving
bull.b: Rapid growth in prescriptions, prescribers, and treated patients indicates early demand for an on-demand PSVT therapy, while expanding formulary coverage improves access. These trends can support repeat use, stronger payer pull-through, and more efficient commercialization over the next several quarters.

bull.t: Cash resources provide a meaningful operating runway
bull.b: The substantial cash position gives Milestone time to advance commercialization, pursue the AFib-RVR program, and work toward additional regulatory decisions without an immediate funding deadline. A runway into H2 2027 supports strategic execution, although it does not yet represent internally generated cash.

bear.t: Severe losses and cash burn remain far ahead of revenue
bear.b: The company is spending heavily while product revenue remains small, creating a substantial gap between operating costs and commercial inflows. Persistent losses and cash outflows could require additional financing before profitability, potentially limiting flexibility and increasing dependence on launch execution.

bear.t: High leverage and declining equity weaken financial resilience
bear.b: Debt of roughly 3.3 times equity leaves a relatively thin capital buffer against continued operating losses. Declining equity reduces balance-sheet resilience, while leverage can constrain future capital allocation and make the company more sensitive to financing conditions as it funds development and commercialization.

bear.t: Revenue growth depends on uncertain reimbursement and trial execution
bear.b: Even with recent access gains, reimbursement timing and payer decisions remain important drivers of realized revenue and average selling price. At the same time, pivotal AFib-RVR execution risks could delay expansion into a larger indication or reduce the value of the development program.
